narrative.h2: Indie video is a budget excuse turned into a style

sections.heading: What indie looks like
sections.body: Indie MV grammar grew from limitations: one camera, one location, one weird idea executed completely. Lo-fi finishes — VHS bleed, expired film stock, blown highlights — are aesthetic choices now, not constraints. The artist often looks slightly bored or amused, never earnest. Composition is loose and asymmetric. Wardrobe is thrifted-looking even when it isn't. The best indie videos feel like they were made by a friend on a Saturday.

sections.heading: Reference points that actually work
sections.body: Tame Impala's 'The Less I Know the Better' directed by Canada is the ceiling — single concept, single set, full commitment. Spike Jonze's videos for Arcade Fire ('The Suburbs') and MGMT ('Time to Pretend') set the high-art end; Michel Gondry's work with The White Stripes ('Fell in Love with a Girl') remains a touchstone. Mac DeMarco's home-shot videos prove a webcam and a backyard can carry a career. Arctic Monkeys' Tranquility Base hotel-themed run added cinematic ambition without losing the slacker tone. Snail Mail, Soccer Mommy, Alvvays, and Mitski's 'Nobody' share the same camera-as-roommate energy. The connective tissue is restraint and a refusal to take the genre too seriously.

sections.heading: Prompting tip for Tunee
sections.body: Pick one idea and stop adding. 'Artist sitting in a backyard kiddie pool for the entire song, slow zoom in across three minutes' is more indie than any elaborate concept. Tunee handles consistent single-location prompts beautifully when you specify the lens — '35mm prime, soft daylight, slight overexposure'. Embrace small mistakes: a boom mic dipping into frame, a passing car. Polish kills the genre faster than a bad song.
